wp2_readout_baseline_addendum.what: Added the calibrated readout-error-mitigation baseline 'linv_calib' (method code in code/vaqem_methods.py: calib_train_indices, calib_pairs, flip_rate_residual, fit_flip_rate, mitigator_linv_calib; wired into run_experiments.all_methods).
wp2_readout_baseline_addendum.why_e2_e3_e5_rerun: all_methods() is called by exp_sweep (E2) and exp_calib (E5), so those two were regenerated; E3 was regenerated as a determinism control and came out byte-identical (exp_shots does not call all_methods and carries no linv_calib rows).
wp2_readout_baseline_addendum.acceptance_e2: final_sweep.json 992 -> 1056 rows: 64 added, all method 'linv_calib' (16 settings x 4 shot budgets); 0 removed; 0 changed. Every pre-existing number is byte-identical to the pre-WP2 archive.
wp2_readout_baseline_addendum.acceptance_e5: e5_calib.json 288 -> 306 rows: 18 added, all 'linv_calib'; 0 removed; the 288 shared rows differ only in the wall-clock fields t_fit_s/t_retrain_s, no scientific field changed.
wp2_readout_baseline_addendum.why_e4_not_rerun: e4_scaling.json carries the cold-cache wall-clock measurements t_data_s/t_oracle_s that paper/check_tex.py:check_costs audits, and that check deliberately FAILS when the scaling rows report data_from_cache. A warm-cache re-run would replace a simulation cost with a cache-lookup time, and splicing freshly timed linv_calib rows into the archived file would mix two cache provenances inside one file. E4 therefore keeps its archived contents and has no linv_calib rows; the readout baseline is compared in E2, E3 and E5, where provenance is uniform.
wp2_readout_baseline_addendum.environment_note: autograd must be >= 1.9: vaqem_lib.gate_real_block uses plain-numpy cos/sin so that autograd.grad can differentiate the statevector simulation, which needs ArrayBox.__array_ufunc__ (absent in 1.8.0). See requirements.txt.
wp2_readout_baseline_addendum.stability_note: run_experiments.py sweep was observed to die with an intermittent SIGSEGV at a varying setting when the machine was near memory exhaustion (1-3 GB free, no swap), including once at the default --workers=cpu_count-2=22. It is not reproducible at --workers 6 with the paper parameters (two full 16-setting runs completed, 361.0 s and 5.9 min). The sweep writes its JSON after every setting, so a crash loses only the in-flight setting.
